court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court, Madurai - H.M.O.P. No.96 of 1994
facts_of_case: The parties were related. The husband filed a petition under Section 12(1)(b) and (c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to declare the marriage as a nullity.

legal_principles.principle: Mental capacity is a condition for marriage, and mental disorder renders the marriage voidable.
legal_principles.held: The provision lays down mental capacity as one of the conditions for the marriage and mental disorder renders the marriage voidable.

legal_principles.principle: The prime question to be answered in connection with the validity or otherwise of a marriage is whether the particular person is in a position to comprehend or appreciate the significance of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: The prime question to be answered in connection with the validity or otherwise of a marriage alleged to have been contracted between persons, either of whom is said to be an idiot or insane person, is the question whether the particular person is in a position to comprehend or appreciate the significance of the marriage and its effects and obligations on his status and condition in society.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is against the order of the Family Court Judge, Madurai dated 19.6.1996 made in H.M.O.P. No.96 of 1994.
